description: §49.2.3: a loop condition is a condition (§42.4); `for (a)` on `int | not` is a presence test — admitted.
rationale: §49.2.3: a `while` condition "is a **condition** (§42.4) under the same rule as `if`: a `bool` …, or a bare `T | not` value — a presence test". Provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S460 "a′, go" (supersedes S440 Truthiness Q2 for conditions; keeps S440 #4 = (c), Q1, Gotcha Q2, S442). S478 (bootstrap triage C12): `while` is retired — §49.4.1: "A `while` statement SHALL be rejected with **`E-LOOP-WHILE-RETIRED`**, whose fix-it is `for (cond) { … }` (the same head, the keyword renamed)"; §49.2.3 (S469): the condition rule "applies to the condition head `for (cond)`". Migrated to `for (…)`.
